lessonTitle: Why Google Walled Off Its Own Ad Businesses
pullQuote: When you sit on both sides of a market, the appearance of fairness is a product feature — and you have to build the org chart to protect it.
leadershipTraits: thinks in market perception, not just internal logic
uses org structure to enforce strategy
protects platform neutrality as an asset
situation: On October 18, 2010, Google ad executive Neal Mohan wrote a short internal email explaining why a specific business unit — AdX, Google's ad exchange — had to stay organizationally separate from the buy-side sales team. The stakes: if the same team sold Google's own DSP (called 'Invite') and also pitched competing DSPs to join AdX, those competing DSPs would never trust that AdX was a neutral marketplace. Mohan notes this logic already governed the sell side and had prompted a real org change — moving the Invite team from one manager (Scott) to another (Jason).
insight:
Mohan is protecting what economists call **platform neutrality** — the belief, held by third parties, that a two-sided marketplace does not favor its own products. He flags it as a "HUGE conflict perception," meaning the problem is not just operational; it's reputational. Competing DSPs will only plug into AdX if they believe AdX isn't quietly tilting the field toward Google's own buying tool. The moment one sales team handles both, that belief collapses.

The structural fix — moving Invite to a separate manager — is the point. Mohan isn't writing a policy memo; he's explaining why an org change that already happened was the right call. The lesson is that on a two-sided platform, neutrality cannot just be *claimed*. It has to be made structurally visible. Separation of teams is the proof.
application: If you run a marketplace or platform where you also compete with your own participants — as a supplier, reseller, or tool vendor — draw a hard line in your org chart before your partners draw their own conclusions. Separate the team that serves third-party participants from the team that runs your own competing product. Then tell your partners about the separation explicitly. The structure is the message.
